title: Barnabas (11 June)
hook: son of encouragement, who vouched for Paul when no one else would

segments.voice: Yesterday, Norbert, thrown into the mud by a storm. Your line was knocked from his horse. When your plans fell over, what did you hear? Day nine hundred ninety-nine.

They were all afraid of him, Acts says. Not long ago he was hunting them. He dragged believers out of their houses. Now he has come to Jerusalem saying he has met the risen Jesus on the road. The disciples don't believe he is one of them. Nobody moves toward him. And then one man takes him, and brings him to the apostles, and speaks for him. Today, the man who helped another one stand. Barnabas.
screen: `A ROOM FULL OF FRIGHTENED PEOPLE.` → `A FORMER PERSECUTOR AT THE DOOR.` → `ONE MAN STANDS UP.`

segments.voice: Barnabas wasn't even his first name. Acts introduces him as Joseph, a Levite from Cyprus, whom the apostles nicknamed Barnabas. And Acts translates it for us. In the Douay-Rheims: "The son of consolation." Newer translations say son of encouragement. The Greek word behind it, paraklēsis, can mean comfort, encouragement, or an appeal. A nickname like that is given, not chosen. The first thing we see him do is give: he sells a piece of land and lays the money at the apostles' feet. The second is the scene from the hook. Saul, later called Paul, comes to Jerusalem after his conversion, and the disciples are afraid of him. Acts says they did not believe he was a disciple. Then: "But Barnabas took him, and brought him to the apostles." He tells them Saul's story, the road, the voice, the bold preaching in Damascus. He puts his own name behind a man nobody trusted. Later, when the church at Antioch is growing, it's Barnabas they send, and Acts gives him a one-line portrait: "For he was a good man, and full of the Holy Ghost and of faith." And what does he do there? He goes looking for Saul and brings him to Antioch to teach. Again. Acts is honest that encouragers can disagree. Later Barnabas wants to give a young man named John Mark a second chance after he had left them partway through a journey. Paul refuses. The disagreement is sharp, and they part ways. Barnabas takes Mark anyway. Catholics remember Barnabas as an apostle, though he wasn't one of the Twelve. His gift was seeing what someone could become, and saying so out loud, before anyone else would.
screen: `JOSEPH, NICKNAMED BARNABAS.` · `HE VOUCHES FOR SAUL.` · `A GOOD MAN, FULL OF FAITH.` · `A SECOND CHANCE FOR MARK.` · then, large: `THE SON OF CONSOLATION.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: vouch for someone. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind one person others have written off, or who's new and unsure, or who's trying to start over. Picture them waiting at the edge of a room. Now picture yourself walking over and standing next to them. What would you say about them, honestly, that's good? Find the words. If you pray, you can hold them before God as Barnabas held Saul up before the apostles. If you don't, simply keep their good in mind. The bell holds the time.
Barnabas. The apostles' nickname for Joseph of Cyprus, the son of consolation, who brought Saul in when no one else would.
Your line: son of encouragement. Today, say one good thing about someone to a person who matters to them, while they can hear it, or pass it on later. Day nine hundred ninety-nine.

howItsDone: The Church keeps the memorial of Saint Barnabas, Apostle, on 11 June; at Mass the readings come from Acts, where Barnabas is sent out with Saul from Antioch.

original.note: Greek: comfort, encouragement, appeal — the word in Barnabas's nickname in Acts 4:36.

trapdoor: what you thought: a minor name in the background of Paul's story.
what it means: the man who made Paul's welcome possible, twice.
what a scholar hears: Acts 4:36 glosses his name with paraklēsis, which older Bibles render consolation and newer ones encouragement.

notes: The index carry 'son of encouragement' is the modern rendering; Douay-Rheims and KJV read 'son of consolation'. Script says so plainly.
paraklēsis gloss (comfort, encouragement, appeal) and pronunciation: confirm.
'Catholics remember Barnabas as an apostle, though he wasn't one of the Twelve': based on Acts 14:14 and the liturgical title 'Apostle'; confirm.
'Barnabas wasn't even his first name': Acts 4:36 names him Joseph; confirm phrasing.
Review picks up day 998 (Norbert), which was written in this same batch.

Editor: hook rebuilt from Acts 9:26–27 (opens on the text, drops the invented 'by the arm' and 'walks him to the front' and the third Yesterday/Today contrast in a row); cut speculation about why the apostles chose the nickname; Acts 8:3 added for 'dragged believers out of their houses'.
Audit: Acts 4:37 says 'land', not 'a field'; 'the push that gets someone on their feet' (a preacher's gloss) replaced with the lexicon senses of paraklēsis.
